name: C2PA Content Credentials
description: Checks for C2PA (Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity) content credentials and provenance data. The C2PA standard provides cryptographic proof of content origin and edit history, enabling verifiable chain of custody from capture to publication.
mechanism:
The C2PA verification process involves multiple stages:

1. **JUMBF Container Detection**: Scans the image binary for JUMBF (JPEG Universal Metadata Box Format) superboxes, which are the transport mechanism for C2PA manifests.

2. **CBOR Payload Parsing**: Extracts and decodes CBOR (Concise Binary Object Representation) payloads containing claim data, assertions, and credential stores.

3. **AI Action Detection**: Searches for action declarations that indicate AI generation, including `c2pa.created`, `ai_generated`, `trainedAlgorithmicMedia`, and `compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia`.

4. **Provenance Chain Validation**: Traces the manifest chain to establish origin — whether the image was captured by a compliant camera, edited in a C2PA-aware editor, or generated by an AI tool that declares its output.
parameters:
C2PA markers: content credentials, manifest store, JUMBF superbox, CBOR containers
AI action types: c2pa.created, ai_generated, trainedAlgorithmicMedia
Supported cameras: Leica M11, Sony α7/α9 series, Nikon Z series
Supported editors: Adobe Photoshop 2024+, Lightroom, Truepic
accuracy: Very High - 95%+ when C2PA data is present. Currently limited adoption (~5% of all images). As adoption grows (Adobe, Google, Microsoft, BBC), this will become a primary verification method.
source: C2PA Technical Specification 2.0, Content Authenticity Initiative (CAI)
useCase: Primary verification for images from C2PA-compliant sources such as news organizations, professional photography, and AI platforms that implement content credentials. Essential for media provenance verification in journalism and content moderation workflows.
strengths:
• Cryptographic proof of origin — cannot be easily forged
• Complete edit history from capture to publication
• Industry-backed standard (Adobe, Microsoft, Google, BBC, Intel)
• Covers both AI-generated and camera-captured content
• Machine-readable and human-verifiable
limitations:
• Very low adoption rate currently (~5% of images)
• Metadata can be stripped during sharing on social media
• Requires C2PA-compliant hardware or software at capture/creation
• Does not prevent screenshot-based circumvention
• Standard is still evolving — version compatibility issues
